issue.title: SASE Claude agents accept unaudited cross-session messages from any bypass-mode Claude session and expose async tools that cannot deliver in a single turn
issue.description: Closing Claude Code's native cross-session messaging side channel for SASE agents and removing vendor async tools; found while consolidating multi-agent collaboration research.

task_type_fields.impact: Impact: an unaudited peer-steering path into every running SASE Claude agent, which bypasses host-owned provenance and completion rules. A message "never counts as consent", but in bypass mode no prompt gates the actions it requests. The exposed async tools let an agent start work whose result can never return in a single-turn run. Context and recommendation: research:202609/multi_agent_collaboration_strategy/multi_agent_collaboration_strategy.md §3.3 and §6.2 (Stage 0).
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/llm_provider/claude.py:412-427 (claude -p launch args: --disallowedTools ScheduleWakeup only, no crossSessionInbound)
task_type_fields.repro:
Root cause: `ClaudeProvider` launches every SASE Claude agent as `claude -p ... --dangerously-skip-permissions --disallowedTools ScheduleWakeup` (src/sase/llm_provider/claude.py:412-427) and sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` (claude.py:527), but passes no `crossSessionInbound` setting and no deny for `ListAgents`. Claude Code >= 2.1.224 binds a cross-session inbox socket for `claude -p` sessions, and per https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging a receiving session that bypasses permissions delivers a peer message whenever the sender also bypasses. Every SASE Claude agent bypasses, so any SASE Claude agent (or any `--dangerously-skip-permissions` Claude session the user runs by hand) can inject text into another SASE agent's running turn "between tool calls", and nothing reaches SASE chats, artifacts, or audit.

Reproduction (2026-09-22, sase 8acb66c44, Claude Code 2.1.278, inside a SASE-launched Claude agent on athena):
1. `env | grep CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING` shows `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET=/run/user/1000/cc-socks/<pid>.sock` and a token.
2. Calling the `ListAgents` tool names this session (`sase-29-4e`) and lists a live peer session (`sase-25-ae`).
3. The same session's tool list also exposes `Workflow`, `Monitor`, `CronCreate`/`CronDelete`, and `RemoteTrigger`, whose results arrive via background task-notifications or later wakeups that can never reach a single-turn SASE run; `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` does not remove them.
Independent earlier observation: research agent research.26.cld reported the same socket plus three live peers on 2026-09-21. Run-archive scan (2026-08-15..09-22, 4,819 tool_calls.jsonl logs): 1 `SendMessage` call and 75 `ListAgents` calls in 22 runs, the sampled ones from epic phase workers.

Suggested fix: pass `--settings '{"crossSessionInbound":"refuse"}'` (a `--settings` value outranks user settings) and add `ListAgents`, `Workflow`, `Monitor`, `CronCreate`, `CronDelete`, `RemoteTrigger` to `--disallowedTools`. Keep `SendMessage` allowed, because denying it also removes in-session subagent messaging. Add a provider-args unit test. Note that the SASE host cannot use this socket as a transport anyway: the runner is Claude's parent, not an own-child, so host posts would be held and expire after 5 minutes in `-p`.

payload.entry: Critique correction (research.26.critique; see research:202609/multi_agent_collaboration_strategy/multi_agent_collaboration_strategy__critique.md, finding m1): the fix stands, but the async-tool rationale is inaccurate. Per code.claude.com/docs/en/headless, claude -p stays open until background subagents or workflows finish (capped at 10 min by CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS), and a Monitor watch keeps feeding output mid-turn in -p. SASE loses those results because the final declaration comes last and its provider teardown watchdog (68d9e0f65) terminates the provider 120s after the declaration is accepted. Implementation notes: dedicated switches CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 exist (--disallowedTools also works). crossSessionInbound=refuse also refuses the session's own hook and Bash socket posts, and a stricter project/local .claude/settings.json value overrides --settings. Peer messages appear on stream-json output as origin.kind="peer", which could be logged as an audit tripwire.
